title: CLI extensions SDK playbook — notes and quickstart skeleton
body:
Purpose:
This is a working playbook for a lightweight, discoverable CLI plugin/extension model for the Redwood SDKs (initial focus: node + python CLIs). Goal: make it easy for product engineers and third-party integrators to add commands, generators, and deployment helpers without changing core SDKs.

Notes to self / design goals (high-level):
- Zero-install experience for most users: core CLI should have a plugin manager that can fetch and run plugins from a registry or local path.
- Clear security model: signed manifests, capability scoping (eg. network access, cloud creds), sandboxing for untrusted plugins.
- Version compatibility: plugin manifests declare compatible CLI versions and minimum runtime.
- UX: discoverability via `rw plugin list`, searchable descriptions, `rw plugin init TEMPLATE` generators.
- Extensibility targets: code generators, model packaging helpers, deployment adapters (k8s/terraform), monitoring hooks (prometheus dashboards), eval/bench wrappers.

Who this is for:
- Internal SDK team: implement plugin host, registry proto, docs and quickstarts.
- Solutions & SE: author example plugins for customer integrations.
- Community contributors: allow external plugins with clear security boundaries.

Plugin model (sketch):
- Plugin package layout (python):
  - rw_plugin.json (manifest)
  - bin/ (executable entry points)
  - templates/ (generator templates)
  - hooks/ (optional lifecycle hooks)
  - README.md

- Manifest fields (rw_plugin.json) — minimal:
  {
    "name": "string",
    "version": "semver",
    "cli_compat": ">=1.4.0 <2.0.0",
    "entrypoints": ["list","deploy","init"],
    "capabilities": ["network","file-write"],
    "description": "short text",
    "repository": "url"
  }

Quickstart skeleton (developer flow) — target: <10 min to scaffold+run example plugin locally:
1) Install local dev CLI: `pipx install rw-cli==1.4.2` or `npm i -g @redwood/rw-cli@1.4.2`
2) Scaffold plugin: `rw plugin create my-sample-plugin --lang python --template generator` // creates a skeleton with rw_plugin.json, example template, tests
3) Link plugin for local dev: `rw plugin link ./my-sample-plugin` (adds to ~/.rw/plugins.json)
4) Run discovery: `rw plugin list` -> shows linked plugin with short desc
5) Try generator: `rw plugin run my-sample-plugin init --name hello-redwood` -> outputs scaffolded folder
6) Publish (later): `rw plugin publish --registry https://plugins.redwood.ai`

Developer checklist (first-pass implementation):
- [ ] Plugin manifest parser in CLI core (strict validation + helpful error messages)
- [ ] Local linking and unlinking UX (dev mode)
- [ ] Remote registry proto (index, search, download) + minimal registry service (S3 + index)
- [ ] Offline install from tarball
- [ ] Entrypoints: command registration API (name, help, args)
- [ ] Execution sandbox (spawn in new process, limit env propagation)
- [ ] Capability checks (prompt or block if plugin requests network/file access)
- [ ] Basic plugin signing + signature verification on install/publish
- [ ] Tests: unit for manifest, e2e for linking+running sample plugin
- [ ] Docs: quickstart, plugin authoring guide, security model doc

Security/Trust model (open questions):
- How strict should the default be? Block network access unless explicit? Prompt on install?
- For enterprise/private deployments we should allow an allowlist-only mode: only org-approved plugins can be installed.
- Signing: initial approach: GPG or RSA signatures tied to GitHub org; longer-term: OCI registry with signed artifacts.

Example plugin use cases (internal seed plugins):
- `rw-plugin-eval-runner`: wraps Redwood eval harness, uploads metrics to Redwood Optimize.
- `rw-plugin-k8s-deploy`: translates `rw deploy` into Helm chart + image build steps tuned for Dedicated.
- `rw-plugin-conftest`: injects deployment-time policy checks (security/compliance) before deploy.
- `rw-plugin-templates`: project templates for common Redwood use-cases (chat-assistant, search-retrieval, embedding-pipeline).

Docs outline (for website + drive):
- Getting started for plugin authors (code walkthrough)
- Plugin manifest reference (fields + examples)
- Best practices (idempotent commands, tests, telemetry limits)
- Security guide (capabilities, signing, enterprise allowlist)
- Publishing guide (registry API, semantic versioning)
- Troubleshooting guide (common errors and how to fix)

UX notes / CLI ergonomics:
- Prefer `rw plugin install <name>` over `rw plugin add` to be consistent with ecosystem.
- `rw plugin run <plugin> <command> [--] [args]` — keep API stable; allow passing through flags to plugin.
- Show plugin source on `rw plugin info <name>` (linked repo, version, hash).
- Deprecation path: plugins declare deprecated entrypoints; core CLI surfaces warnings.

Telemetry & privacy:
- Core CLI should emit minimal telemetry by default: plugin name, success/failure, duration. Mask any PII.
- Enterprise mode: telemetry off by default; opt-in to send metrics to Redwood.

Integration testing approach:
- Provide `rw plugin test` harness that runs plugin in ephemeral container (or VM) against mocked Redwood endpoints.
- CI jobs: each plugin repo should include GH actions that run the harness and CLI compliance checks (linting of manifest, license file, small smoke test).

Open questions / decisions to make (next meeting):
- Registry: build simple S3 index vs adopt an existing package registry (npm/pypi/OCI). Pros/cons list needed.
- Signing mechanism and key management for org-published plugins.
- Scope model: how granular should capabilities be? per-command or per-plugin?
- Do we want to support multiple languages out of the box or provide a thin shim system?

Next milestones (2-week cadence):
- Week 0–2: prototype manifest parser + local link/run for python plugin (MVP)
- Week 2–4: public quickstart doc + two seed plugins (templates + eval-runner)
- Week 4–6: add registry index prototype + publish flow; initial security doc draft
- Week 6–8: GH actions harness, CI checks, sample registry integration

Notes for authoring the doc page on Drive (this file):
- Keep this as an engineering working doc — short bullets, TODOs, and links back to PRs and Confluence.
- After Week 4, promote a polished Authoring Guide in docs.redwood.ai and move the playbook to a confluence canonical page for the SDK team.

Quick debugging tips (handy commands for devs):
- `RW_DEBUG=1 rw plugin run my-sample-plugin deploy --target local` -> verbose logs
- `rw plugin inspect ./my-sample-plugin` -> prints manifest and entrypoints
- `rw plugin validate-manifest rw_plugin.json` -> quick lint
- `rw plugin run --sandbox=off` -> skip sandbox for trusted local debugging

Random ideas (brain dump):
- Plugin marketplace badges (verified, org-approved)
- CLI interactive mode to walk users through install+capability prompts
- `rw plugin migrate` to help upgrade plugin manifests when CLI bumps major version

Unresolved TODOs in this doc:
- Decide registry proto (S3 index vs OCI). (assigned: Evan)
- Draft initial manifest schema JSON schema file. (assigned: Priya)
- Put together seed plugin repos and link to this doc. (assigned: Samir)

End of notes.
